detailed_rationale:
Waaree Renewable Technologies (WRTL) is the solar EPC (engineering, procurement, construction) arm within the wider Waaree group (separate from listed module manufacturer Waaree Energies). Q1 FY27 (June-2026 quarter) revenue rose 53.2% YoY to Rs 924.25 crore and consolidated net profit rose 34-38% YoY to ~Rs 117-119 crore. EBITDA margin eased slightly to 18.77% from 19.49% a year earlier -- management characterized this as a deliberate outcome of selective, disciplined bidding to protect a stated full-year EBITDA margin floor of ~15%, rather than a sign of deteriorating pricing power, which is a materially different (and more benign) explanation than the margin compression peers like Saatvik Green Energy reported the same quarter. The company entered the quarter with an unexecuted EPC order book of 2.92 GWp / more than Rs 5,300 crore, providing good multi-quarter revenue visibility.

A notable strategic development: WRTL completed the ~Rs 1,225 crore acquisition of a 55% stake in Associated Power Structures Private Limited (APSPL) on 18-June-2026, giving it backward integration into transmission and grid (T&D) infrastructure -- a genuine structural move to address the solar-evacuation bottleneck that has periodically constrained utility-scale project completion in India, and to access a reported ~Rs 20,000 crore T&D bidding pipeline. This diversifies WRTL's growth drivers beyond pure solar EPC execution.

Balance sheet is strong (D/E ~0.16, interest coverage ~49x) and returns are excellent (ROE ~26.5%, ROCE ~38.75%). The very high trailing revenue growth (108-112% per the quant sheet, 3yr and 1yr) reflects a company scaling rapidly during India's solar capacity boom from what was a much smaller base a few years ago -- a genuine business ramp, but not a rate that can mechanically repeat once the order book normalizes to a larger revenue base.
recommendation_rationale: Quant already rates this Hold on both horizons (final scores 74.1/63.2) despite an excellent quality_score (~94); the trailing 100%+ growth figures are a scaling-base artifact that should not be extrapolated, and while the APSPL move and disciplined-bidding margin story are both genuinely constructive, they support holding a well-run compounder at a fair price rather than justifying a rescue upgrade.
summary: Waaree Renewable Technologies is the solar EPC business within the Waaree group, growing fast on the back of India's solar capacity build-out, with a large and growing order book and excellent returns on capital. Management has also moved to acquire a transmission-infrastructure company, addressing a real bottleneck (grid connection delays) for solar projects. The very high trailing growth rates reflect rapid scaling from a smaller base and should not be assumed to continue at the same pace, but the underlying business looks well-managed. We rate it a Hold.
positive_para: A large order book (2.92 GWp / >Rs 5,300 crore) gives strong multi-quarter revenue visibility, returns on capital are excellent (ROCE ~39%), and the disciplined-bidding explanation for the modest margin dip (with a stated 15% EBITDA floor) is a materially healthier signal than outright margin compression. The APSPL acquisition is a genuine structural move into grid/transmission infrastructure that both reduces a real project-completion risk (evacuation bottlenecks) and opens a large incremental addressable market.
negative_para: Trailing 3-year and 1-year revenue growth of 108-112% is a base-effect of rapid scaling and mathematically cannot continue at that rate as the revenue base grows; EPC is also an inherently lower-margin, execution-risk business relative to manufacturing, and the newly acquired APSPL brings integration risk and a different (grid/transmission) regulatory and execution environment that WRTL has not previously operated in at this scale.
reverse_dcf_judgment: At a ~Rs 10,474 crore market cap and trailing PE of ~21.9x against ROCE near 39%, the market is pricing continued strong (not hypergrowth) execution -- reasonable given the order book and the T&D diversification, but not a bargain given how much of the historical growth rate is a scaling artifact that will mathematically decelerate. Call: fair value for a well-run, high-return EPC platform now diversifying into grid infrastructure.
